MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Record keeping in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Record keeping in aquaculture.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Record keeping in aquaculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Record keeping in aquaculture.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Reproduction.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish Reproduction.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Reproduction.

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Paper burning to ash

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish feeds and feeding? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish feeds and feeding.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fish feeds and feeding.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish feeds and feeding.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of marine and freshwater environments? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Fish Reproduction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Fish Ecology and Ecosystems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Ornamental Fish culture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Record keeping in aquaculture.

2. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Reproduction.

3. C — Glucose and oxygen

4. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

5. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. A — Ice melting to water

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish feeds and feeding.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Buoyancy, locomotion and movement in fishes.

9. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and osmoregulation in fishes.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

12. B — newton (N)

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Fish Ecology and Ecosystems; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
